reasoning_content:
pip is successfully fetching from PyPI while silently failing to resolve the extra index URL with the redacted placeholder. The issue is that `@` isn't valid in a hostname per RFC 3986, but urllib seems to be tolerating it in practice, allowing the build to continue.

Now I'm setting up a build matrix across 30 Dockerfiles — 24 backend services, 1 shared service, 5 frontend, and 1 additional. Most are straightforward, but the dokumentenaufbereitung-monorepo has a massive model download step from HuggingFace and GitHub that could balloon the build to several GB and consume most of the available memory, so I need to be careful with that one.

The tex2pdf-service is a workspace project with a root pyproject.toml and member packages under src/api, src/cli, and src/core — the Dockerfile syncs from the root and installs editable packages from the subdirectories. I've already generated a root uv.lock, but I need to verify whether the member packages have their own pyproject files and whether uv lock covers the entire workspace properly.

For the demospipes builds, I'm using the monorepo root as context and applying sed to replace the base image tags with local references. I need to be mindful of the 600-second timeout per command and manage memory constraints — running builds in the foreground with output to a log file is the safest approach since background processes could get killed.

My build strategy is to sequence them by complexity: start with quick validation on a few representative services, then batch the simpler ones, handle the heavier services (tex2pdf, dokumentenaufbereitung-monorepo) individually, and finish with the frontend last. I also need to check which services have a scripts directory since some Dockerfiles copy it, and verify the full content of the report config.

Before building, I should verify the demospipes addon context — the Dockerfiles expect to copy from subdirectories like `api/` and `executors/`, so I need to confirm the build context is the addons root and those directories exist there. I also need to make sure the `uv.lock` file is present where the Dockerfile expects it for the addon dependencies.

I'm planning to batch the first build wave: running dokumentenpruefung, kommentar-service, and ki-validierung with appropriate secrets and context. Since I don't know the build times, I'll start with a single build first, then parallelize from there.

Now I'm setting up the batch builds — dokumentenpruefung from the monorepo root, ki-validierung from its own directory, and kommentar-service with the uv.lock file copied into context. I'll run these with a 570-second timeout per build, writing logs to /tmp.
